rationale: This is a cosmetic variant of the archived DeepValueTrapScreen — same gate-times-profitability geometry, same grading channel, with only a highly correlated cheapness proxy (EBITDA/P vs OCF/P) substituted and the threshold simultaneously moved from 0.7 to 0.6, so it neither isolates one design choice nor introduces a new economic mechanism.

Still the same template as the archived winner, but replacing equity-based cheapness with a strictly-positive enterprise-yield gate addresses a genuine confound (leverage) that all prior archive gates share, and the expression cleanly matches the stated hypothesis.

The level-vs-persistence question is worth asking, but every other archive use of INDICATOR takes a cross-sectional rank/quantile as its second argument, so INDICATOR(RATIO(oiadp,at), 0.02) is likely to be read as a ~2nd-percentile threshold and return 1 for nearly all firms, making TS_SUM a near-constant with almost no cross-sectional dispersion.

Gating on sales-to-price and then sorting on operating margin selects almost exactly the high-earnings-yield firms, so the long leg is a rediscovery of the E/P anomaly dressed as a two-channel interaction, and the archive already found the closely related P/S-times-margin construction unproductive.

The dividend-yield gate is a genuinely fresh valuation channel, but the grading term (oiadp − dvc)/at is numerically dominated by ROA since dvc/at is typically an order of magnitude smaller, so the expression does not actually measure payout coverage as the hypothesis claims and reduces to yield-gated profitability.

Capital intensity of profits is a legitimately novel and plausibly FF5-orthogonal grading channel, but dp/oibdp flips sign whenever operating profit is negative — common among cheap value firms and far more than 2% of the gated sample — so NEG(WINSOR(...)) will systematically award top scores to loss-making firms, contradicting the stated mechanism.
